title: Borrowed Corner
designBriefSource: The requested six-family planning batch; private prompt retained outside distribution.
goal: Collect the gem at (7,3,0) after usable L-tool delivery and subsequent target work.
stageDependency: Retreat the tool downward -> use the released cross-aisle to park the shutter -> recover the tool upward -> dock from the supported side -> transmit lateral contact -> lift and shift the target to expose the gem.
planningBurden: Advancing the tool immediately blocks the helper input. The lower parking bay must preserve extraction, and the delivered tool must leave the target usable.
changedConstraints: One long shutter and an asymmetric L replace the source multi-helper workspace.
A side corridor makes retreat before shutter movement necessary.
A second visible void removes a discovered axial-input bypass while preserving supported tool movement.
Two post-contact target operations preserve a complete final objective.
physicalScope: One 16 by 16 room; ordinary pinned official engine; all initial actors at elevation zero.

difficulty.qualification: An author estimate from dependent operations and planning tradeoffs, not calibrated human difficulty.

limits: All three groups, lateral transfer, preparation, downward/upward tool motion, ordered retreat-and-recovery, and post-contact target work pass exhausted checks.
The exact witness, helper parking location and minimal tool silhouette are not proved unique.
